description:
An artifact outside the development root is retained where it is rather than copied into the archive, and artifact discovery stops following links at such an artifact instead of walking through it.

## Background

Classification picks an action from two independent flags: whether the plan wants a destination for the artifact, and whether it needs the source kept. Wanting a destination while keeping the source yields a copy; keeping the source without wanting a destination yields a retention, which is an action the planner already produces.

Treating an artifact outside the development root as permanent was introduced so that such an artifact would stop blocking a plan. Permanence was designed for a living-documentation area, where the archive genuinely wants a frozen snapshot and readers keep the live file, so it sets the keep-the-source flag and leaves the wants-a-destination flag true. The copying that follows for out-of-root artifacts is an inherited consequence rather than a chosen behaviour.

Discovery compounds it. The artifact graph is an unbounded transitive closure: every local link in every artifact is resolved, its target is enqueued as an embedded artifact, and the walk repeats until the frontier closes. The adopter documentation set is densely cross-linked and several repository-root files are hubs within it, so one linked document that cites a hub pulls the entire set into that container's plan. Measured over this repository's terminal containers, four explicitly linked documents in one container yield 91 embedded artifacts, and the containers together schedule 684 copy operations over 139 distinct files.

Neither change removes a relocation. Every artifact the current plans schedule for relocation is reached without walking through an artifact that lies outside the development root.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: An artifact whose source lies outside the configured development root is retained: the plan schedules no destination for it and its source is left in place.
- [hard] REQ-02: An artifact under a configured permanent area inside the development root is still copied, with its source retained.
- [hard] REQ-03: A retained out-of-root artifact contributes no descendants to the plan: no artifact reached only through that artifact's links appears in the plan. The artifact itself still enters the plan when a scanned artifact links it.
- [hard] REQ-04: Every artifact that the preceding classification scheduled for relocation is still scheduled for relocation, and no relocation becomes a retention or a copy.
- [hard] REQ-05: A plan reports no unmanaged-selected-root blocker for a document linked at a source, script, agent-asset, or repository-root path.

## Notes

REQ-05 preserves the outcome that classifying out-of-root artifacts as permanent was introduced to deliver; it is restated here because this change replaces the mechanism that delivers it.

REQ-04 is the load-bearing safety property. The two changes are independent in principle — one alters an action, the other bounds a walk — and either one alone could silently drop an artifact from a plan if the interaction is not measured against the preceding behaviour.

REQ-03 was amended at the owner's direction after implementation measured the alternative. Requiring discovery to stop *reading* at the boundary, rather than to stop contributing descendants, bounds the ownership walk as well: 8 artifacts lose the `outside-owner` evidence they derive from chains running through an out-of-root artifact, flip from copy to relocation, and are deleted from live locations that another issue's document still reaches. REQ-04's letter permits that, which is why the criterion rather than the implementation was the thing to correct.
title: Retain artifacts outside the development root and stop discovery at them
